Registered Agent & Physical Address Licensed Agent Required

A virtual office is generally permissible as the registered address for a Spanish SL if it provides a genuine physical location for service of process, official communications, and mail collection. However, for this ISIC 4638 export distribution business, the virtual office must be supplemented with documentation evidencing commercial substance in Spain, such as management meetings, contracts, accounting files, and correspondence. Pure mail-forwarding without any local staff or accounting presence may be treated as a letterbox arrangement by the Agencia Tributaria, leading to VAT registration challenges or economic presence assertions.

Stage 02

Statutory Formation & Board Resolutions

Competent registry, governing statute, capital lockup rules, and first board resolution template.

Competent corporate registry

Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) for the name certificate; Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province of the registered office for the inscription; oversight by the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (Ministry of Justice).

Governing statute

Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, Ley de Sociedades de Capital (Capital Companies Act), Articles 4, 20-22, 23-29, 58-66, 210-221; Código de Comercio; Reglamento del Registro Mercantil (Royal Decree 1784/1996); Law 14/2013 supporting entrepreneurship measures

Formation / constitutional filings

Escritura Pública de Constitución (notarial public deed of incorporation) with annexed Bylaws (Estatutos Sociales), to be filed as Inscripción 1ª in the Registro Mercantil Provincial.

Incorporation processing time

⚡ 53 business days (SOP sum)

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime Mandatory Capital Deposit & Lockup

EUR 3,000 minimum share capital, fully subscribed and fully paid at execution of the deed (Article 4 LSC). Cash contributions must be deposited in a Spanish bank account opened in the company's name before incorporation, with the bank issuing a blocked capital deposit certificate annexed to the deed; the funds remain blocked until the registration is granted. Non-cash contributions must be described in the deed and supported by an expert valuation report. Alternative: Sociedad Limitada de Formación Sucesiva may be incorporated with EUR 1, retaining 20% of profits until the capital reaches EUR 3,000.

Funding & unlock path: Fire safety clearance under CTE DB-SI (Royal Decree 314/2006) including fire extinguishers, emergency exits, fire doors, and the classified storage area for combustible tallow-based products; structural load clearance by a competent architect confirming the warehouse floor capacity and racking installation reviewed under UNE-EN 15635; electrical installation certificate under RD 842/2002 (REBT); occupational health and safety risk assessment and preventive service under Law 31/1995 and RD 39/1997, including forklift operator training and worker welfare facilities; food safety plan with HACCP and traceability per Regulation (EC) 852/2004; and the municipal first-occupancy and activity certificate confirming the premises are fit for the licensed use.

Paid-in capital rule: EUR 3,000 minimum share capital, fully subscribed and fully paid at execution of the deed (Article 4 LSC). Cash contributions must be deposited in a Spanish bank account opened in the company's name before incorporation, with the bank issuing a blocked capital deposit certificate annexed to the deed; the funds remain blocked until the registration is granted. Non-cash contributions must be described in the deed and supported by an expert valuation report. Alternative: Sociedad Limitada de Formación Sucesiva may be incorporated with EUR 1, retaining 20% of profits until the capital reaches EUR 3,000.

Pro-Forma First Board Resolution Draft
FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION. WHEREAS the founders have executed the public deed of incorporation, adopting the Bylaws, and the registered capital of EUR 3,000 has been fully subscribed and paid. NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED: (1) the share subscription made in the deed is ratified and allocated; (2) the registered address fixed in the Bylaws is adopted as the legal seat; (3) the named administrators are confirmed in office, effective upon commercial registration; and (4) the administrators are expressly authorized to open bank accounts, apply for the provisional NIF, pay the AJD tax and registry fees, and execute all documents necessary to obtain inscription in the Mercantile Registry.
Industrial Access / EIA & Civil Defense Approval Mandatory Environmental Clearance

Ministerio de Industria y Turismo, Dirección General de Industria y de la PYME; Consejería de Industria of the relevant Autonomous Community; Spanish Agency for Food Safety and Nutrition (AESAN) through the regional health authorities; and the municipal Town Hall for the opening license.

Category: Municipal Opening and Activity Licence (Licencia de Apertura y Funcionamiento) for the storage and distribution warehouse, together with registration in the Registro General Sanitario de Empresas Alimentarias y Alimentos (RGSEAA) under the category 'wholesale trade and distribution of food products'.

Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) - Sede Electrónica at https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es (national tax portal covering corporate tax, VAT, census registration, SII e-invoicing and customs via the Ventanilla Única Aduanera / ECS system)

E-government filing portal

For the Spanish SL (ES_SL): the NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) is the company tax identification code, issued by AEAT at incorporation through the notary; the notary obtains a provisional NIF and the definitive NIF is confirmed once the SL is inscribed in the Registro Mercantil. The SL must file Form 036 (censo de empresarios, profesionales y retenedores) to activate VAT registration, obtain the NIF-IVA (Spanish VAT number in EU format ES + NIF), and obtain an EORI-ES customs registration number for export declarations in the ECS. For a foreign entity without a permanent establishment: apply to AEAT using Form 036 with box 615/616, appointing a fiscal representative resident in Spain and attaching the certificate of incorporation, legal representative power of attorney, passport, and Spanish translation with apostille/legalisation; the non-resident NIF is issued for owning Spanish assets or performing taxable activities, and the foreign company must also register for EORI if it exports goods in its own name. There is no government fee for the NIF, but notarial and registry fees apply for the SL; foreign entities carrying on cross-border food wholesale must complete registration before the first supply in Spain.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation - The Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada is a Spanish-resident corporate taxpayer subject to Impuesto sobre Sociedades (IS) at the general fixed rate of 25% (with a reduced 15% rate for the first two tax years where the SL is newly created, carries on an activity and has turnover below EUR 1,000,000). Retained profits are taxed at entity level; dividend distributions to non-resident shareholders are subject to withholding tax under Impuesto sobre la Renta de No Residentes (IRNR), generally 19% for EU/EEA residents and 21% for other jurisdictions, subject to treaty relief. A non-resident shareholder with no permanent establishment is not otherwise subject to Spanish corporation tax. — For the Spanish SL (ES_SL): the NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) is the company tax identification code, issued by AEAT at incorporation through the notary; the notary obtains a provisional NIF and the definitive NIF is confirmed once the SL is inscribed in the Registro Mercantil. The SL must file Form 036 (censo de empresarios, profesionales y retenedores) to activate VAT registration, obtain the NIF-IVA (Spanish VAT number in EU format ES + NIF), and obtain an EORI-ES customs registration number for export declarations in the ECS. For a foreign entity without a permanent establishment: apply to AEAT using Form 036 with box 615/616, appointing a fiscal representative resident in Spain and attaching the certificate of incorporation, legal representative power of attorney, passport, and Spanish translation with apostille/legalisation; the non-resident NIF is issued for owning Spanish assets or performing taxable activities, and the foreign company must also register for EORI if it exports goods in its own name. There is no government fee for the NIF, but notarial and registry fees apply for the SL; foreign entities carrying on cross-border food wholesale must complete registration before the first supply in Spain.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation - The Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada is a Spanish-resident corporate taxpayer subject to Impuesto sobre Sociedades (IS) at the general fixed rate of 25% (with a reduced 15% rate for the first two tax years where the SL is newly created, carries on an activity and has turnover below EUR 1,000,000). Retained profits are taxed at entity level; dividend distributions to non-resident shareholders are subject to withholding tax under Impuesto sobre la Renta de No Residentes (IRNR), generally 19% for EU/EEA residents and 21% for other jurisdictions, subject to treaty relief. A non-resident shareholder with no permanent establishment is not otherwise subject to Spanish corporation tax.

Available election forms

Spain does not operate a check-the-box election; an SL is mandatorily a capital company under civil law and cannot be treated as transparent for Spanish tax purposes. Available elections include: (i) the reduced 15% IS rate for newly created SLs if the business activity is started during that tax period and turnover does not exceed EUR 1,000,000; (ii) the optional consolidated tax group (grupo fiscal) for a Spanish parent with at least 70% shareholding (75% for listed groups); (iii) the optional VAT group regime (régimen especial de grupo de entidades) for VAT consolidation; (iv) transfer-pricing advance pricing agreements (APAs) with AEAT; (v) the patent box regime for qualifying intangibles (Art. 23 Ley del Impuesto sobre Sociedades, 27/2014); (vi) the special tax-neutral reorganisation regime (Art. 76 LIS) for mergers and spin-offs; and (vii) the special Canary Islands (ZEC) economic zone regime. Hybrid mismatch rules under ATAD (Directive 2016/1164/EU as implemented) apply mandatorily and cannot be disapplied by election.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

No general de minimis turnover threshold exists for Spanish-established businesses: any person or entity habitually carrying out an entrepreneurial or professional activity in Spanish territory must file Form 036/037 with AEAT and register for IVA before commencing activity. For non-resident suppliers, registration is required from the first euro of taxable supplies in Spain unless the only trigger is intra-EU distance sales below the EUR 10,000 aggregate pan-European threshold (in which case the supplier is taxed in its Member State of establishment); B2C goods import distance sales may alternatively use the IOSS scheme. Exporters filing monthly VAT returns must join the SII real-time reporting system when their annual turnover exceeds EUR 6,010,121.04.

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

Direct exports of tangible goods by the Spanish SL to a non-EU third country are exempt with right to input VAT deduction at the effective rate of 0% under Art. 21 Ley 37/1992, provided (i) the goods physically leave the EU customs territory, (ii) the exporter holds the validated customs export declaration (DUA/MRN) evidencing the exit office, and (iii) the goods are sold for consideration to a non-resident customer and are not consumed or transformed in Spain before export. Intra-EU dispatches to a buyer with a valid EU VAT number are exempt under Art. 25 LIVA, with the exemption conditioned on the recapitulative statement (Modelo 349) and the buyer's validated VAT ID. For pre-packaged spicy tallow hotpot base bricks (HS 2103.90/2106.90), the export zero-rating applies to the goods themselves; related transport, loading, handling and insurance of the exported goods are also exempt; the exporter should maintain a traceable chain of title and retain the transport document (B/L, airway bill, CMR) confirming the consignment reached a non-EU destination. The exemption is claimed on the VAT return by recording the export invoice operation as exenta, with the full documentation bundle retained for AEAT verification.

  • DUA (Documento Único Administrativo - Customs Export Declaration) transmitted through the Spanish ECS/Ventanilla Única Aduanera with the corresponding MRN and exit-office validation (proof of exit confirmation)
  • Bill of Lading (or Air Waybill / CMR consignment note) evidencing the physical departure of the hotpot soup base from EU customs territory and delivery to the named non-EU consignee
  • Inward Remittance Certificate - bank confirmation / SWIFT MT103 credit advice evidencing receipt of export proceeds in the exporter's Spanish bank account (also required for FX repatriation scrutiny and corporate income tax recognition)
  • Commercial invoice and packing list referencing the MRN, Incoterms 2020, batch numbers, weight and the harmonised system code, and cross-referencing the letter of credit if used
  • Letter of Credit / SWIFT TT payment instruction confirming the transaction value and presenting the transport document as evidence of performance
  • Certificate of origin / EUR.1 or EUR-MED movement certificate, or REX-registered origin declaration where preferential origin is claimed
  • Food hygiene / sanitary export certificate for the foodstuff (heat-treated tallow-based soup base), issued by the competent Spanish authority, and any export licence required for agricultural/food products

Real-time clearance applies through the SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información): taxpayers in the large-company regime (turnover above EUR 6,010,121.04) or those choosing the SII must submit all issued and received invoice records, intra-EU acquisition data and export documentation to AEAT via authenticated web services in XML/SOAP format, with a maximum reporting delay of 4 calendar days from the end of the reporting period (8 calendar days for certain receipts). Other taxpayers file periodical Modelo 303/390 returns with aggregated invoice listings. Spain's e-invoicing mandate under Ley 28/2022 (Ley Crea y Crece) and the Verifactu standard requires all companies to issue electronic invoices (Facturae XML v3.2 preferred) in a machine-readable, tamper-evident format, with phased implementation for B2B transactions; AEAT does not currently impose a central digital-stamping/clearance duty on every document, but SII and Verifactu operate as quasi-real-time fiscal clearance with acceptance of digital certificates, API access and mandatory software certified under the anti-fraud regulation.

AEAT maintains intense scrutiny of export zero-rating due to fraudulent schemes (carousel fraud and false export certificates). Where the required export proof (DUA with exit validation, transport documents, inward payment evidence) is missing or the goods are shown not to have left the EU, AEAT issues a regularisation assessment (acta) clawing back the entire exempt tax, plus late-payment interest (interés de demora). Penalties under Ley 58/2003, de 17 de diciembre, General Tributaria: a material omission or inaccurate return gives a fixed proportional penalty of 50% to 100% of the understated VAT for serious infringement, and 75% to 150% where the infringement involves concealment or is classified as very serious; obtaining an undue tax refund carries a penalty of 100% to 150%; issuing false invoices carries a fine of EUR 1,000 per invoice or, where the false invoice is used by a third party to obtain an undue VAT advantage, up to 50% of the invoice amount. If the defrauded tax exceeds EUR 120,000, the conduct constitutes criminal tax fraud (delito contra la Hacienda Pública) punishable by 2 to 6 years' imprisonment, extended to 6 years and fines up to six times the defrauded amount where the amount exceeds EUR 600,000. The limitation period for VAT assessments is 4 years general, but may extend to 10 years for certain undisclosed offshore structures; in export transactions AEAT enforcement practice requires the exporter to retain the entire documentation bundle (DUA, B/L, bank credits, invoices, SII records) for a minimum of 5 to 6 years and to answer AEAT requests before any export-related VAT refund is paid.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

Spain uses the euro and is subject to EU Treaty free-movement-of-capital rules. Current-account transactions, including imports, exports, service payments, dividends, interest, royalties, and ordinary profit remittances, are generally freely convertible and transferable through regulated payment institutions. Capital-account transactions are also generally unrestricted, subject to anti-money-laundering controls, sanctions screening, prudential rules, tax compliance, and applicable foreign-investment screening or reporting. A Spanish SL may generally remit post-tax profits, dividends, loan repayments, and management charges to non-residents, provided corporate approvals, distributable-profit rules, withholding-tax analysis, beneficial-ownership evidence, transfer-pricing support, and applicable treaty or EU relief conditions are satisfied. Banks may require audited or management accounts, board resolutions, tax-clearance evidence, invoices, contracts, and source-of-funds documentation before executing substantial transfers.

Export proceeds surrender rules

Spain has no general statutory requirement to surrender export proceeds to the Banco de España and no general mandatory conversion ratio or statutory repatriation deadline for export receipts. Export proceeds may normally be retained in euro or foreign-currency accounts and converted when commercially appropriate. Transactions may be subject to balance-of-payments, statistical, tax, customs, bank-compliance, and payment-reporting requirements. The company must retain commercial invoices, customs or transport records, contracts, shipping evidence, and bank confirmations. Cash-payment restrictions, sanctions rules, AML obligations, VAT and customs reporting, and any applicable statistical filings remain applicable. Foreign-investment declarations may be required for qualifying non-resident investments or transactions under Spanish investment-control legislation.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España, operating within the Eurosystem under the European Central Bank; foreign-investment reporting is also administered under the Spanish Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business framework.

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

Cross-border EMI / Fintech rails Fit: High

Medium for payment accounts, collections, SEPA transfers, foreign-exchange execution, and card services; low as a substitute for a full Spanish commercial-bank relationship. An EEA electronic-money institution or payment institution may provide services in Spain through passporting, subject to its home-state authorization, AML controls, safeguarding requirements, and permitted-service scope. An EMI does not provide ordinary bank deposits, deposit-guarantee protection, or necessarily a Spanish IBAN. Offshore non-EEA digital EMIs generally cannot provide regulated payment services into Spain without an appropriate EU authorization, branch, agent, or other lawful basis. The company should maintain a regulated Spanish or EEA bank account for tax payments, payroll, customs, trade-finance support, and counterparties requiring bank-grade evidence.

Core KYC Rejection Triggers & Defense Dossier

Unclear or layered ultimate beneficial ownership, nominee shareholders, bearer-like arrangements, or inability to evidence control of the Spanish SL.

Root cause: Unclear or layered ultimate beneficial ownership, nominee shareholders, bearer-like arrangements, or inability to evidence control of the Spanish SL.

Defense evidence: Current Spanish commercial-registry extract; articles of association; deed of incorporation; shareholder register; ownership chart to natural-person UBOs; passports and residential-address evidence for directors, shareholders, and UBOs; notarized powers of attorney; UBO declaration; and certified corporate documents for foreign shareholders.
Foreign capital injection with no credible source-of-funds or source-of-wealth evidence.

Root cause: Foreign capital injection with no credible source-of-funds or source-of-wealth evidence.

Defense evidence: Bank statements; audited financial statements; tax returns or tax-residency certificates; investor board resolutions; loan agreements; investment agreements; capital-call notices; sale-of-asset records; regulated-bank transfer confirmations; and a written funds-flow memorandum matching each transfer to the subscribed capital or shareholder loan.
Mismatch between the stated wholesale food business and payment activity, counterparties, products, or jurisdictions.

Root cause: Mismatch between the stated wholesale food business and payment activity, counterparties, products, or jurisdictions.

Defense evidence: Business plan; product catalogue; supplier and customer contracts; invoices; customs documentation; transport and warehouse agreements; food-business registrations or required permits; HACCP and food-safety documentation; expected annual turnover; countries of origin and destination; payment-flow map; and transaction-monitoring thresholds.
Transactions involving sanctioned, embargoed, high-risk, or opaque jurisdictions, or counterparties with adverse media or politically exposed-person exposure.

Root cause: Transactions involving sanctioned, embargoed, high-risk, or opaque jurisdictions, or counterparties with adverse media or politically exposed-person exposure.

Defense evidence: Counterparty KYC files; beneficial-owner confirmations; sanctions-screening reports; adverse-media reviews; end-use and end-user statements; shipping-route evidence; certificates of origin; dual-use or sanctions legal analysis where relevant; enhanced due-diligence approval; and documented escalation controls.
Large or unusual cash activity, third-party payments, rapid pass-through transactions, or unexplained round-number transfers.

Root cause: Large or unusual cash activity, third-party payments, rapid pass-through transactions, or unexplained round-number transfers.

Defense evidence: Written treasury policy; prohibition or limitation on cash receipts; approved payment matrix; invoice-to-payment reconciliation; three-way matching records; bank statements; board-approved signatory rules; related-party register; exception logs; and documented commercial rationale for any third-party settlement.
Incomplete tax, customs, VAT, beneficial-ownership, or corporate-registry compliance history.

Root cause: Incomplete tax, customs, VAT, beneficial-ownership, or corporate-registry compliance history.

Defense evidence: Spanish tax identification number; tax-registration evidence; VAT registration where applicable; filed tax returns; customs EORI registration where applicable; annual accounts; corporate tax certificates; registry filings; beneficial-ownership filings; and a compliance calendar showing responsible personnel and filing status.
Foreign-language, expired, uncertified, inconsistent, or unverifiable corporate documentation.

Root cause: Foreign-language, expired, uncertified, inconsistent, or unverifiable corporate documentation.

Defense evidence: Recent certificates issued by competent registries; apostilles or legalization where required; sworn Spanish translations; document-control index; consistency reconciliation across passports, registries, tax records, and ownership charts; and a bank-specific document-validity schedule.

Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

Route subscribed capital or shareholder loans from an account held in the investor's own name at a regulated bank to the Spanish SL's corporate account, using SEPA Credit Transfer for euro payments or SWIFT cross-border transfer for non-euro payments. Include the legal entity name, Spanish IBAN, BIC, payment purpose, capital or loan reference, investor identity, and underlying agreement in the payment narrative. For incorporation capital, obtain the bank's capital-deposit certificate or equivalent evidence required by the notary and commercial registry; the bank may not issue a traditional certificate in every digital-incorporation workflow, so confirm the accepted evidence in advance. For post-incorporation injections, maintain board and shareholder resolutions, subscription or loan agreements, proof of beneficial ownership, source-of-funds evidence, and accounting entries. Apply Spanish foreign-investment reporting where the transaction falls within the applicable reporting categories, including any required declarations under Royal Decree 571/2023 and related Ministry procedures. Reconcile inbound transfers against the general ledger and preserve SWIFT MT103, SEPA confirmation, bank statements, and supporting contracts.Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible euro-area suppliers and SWIFT MT103 for non-SEPA payments. Use commercial documentary letters of credit, preferably confirmed where country or bank risk warrants, for higher-risk imports or new suppliers. The LC file should specify applicant, beneficiary, issuing and advising banks, amount, currency, Incoterms, shipment deadline, documentary requirements, partial-shipment and transshipment rules, insurance, inspection certificates, certificate of origin, commercial invoice, packing list, transport document, and sanctions-screening conditions. Banks may process documentary credits under UCP 600 and documentary collections under URC 522 by contractual incorporation. Match each payment to purchase orders, invoices, customs records, VAT treatment, transport evidence, and supplier due diligence. Avoid third-party settlement unless commercially justified, documented, and pre-cleared by the bank. Maintain maker-checker controls, dual authorization, beneficiary verification, payment limits, sanctions screening, and bank fee or FX-spread monitoring.Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards for documented forecast or committed commercial exposures, subject to bank credit approval, suitability or appropriateness procedures, confirmations, collateral terms, and EMIR-related reporting or risk-mitigation requirements where applicable.Non-deliverable forwards for currencies or jurisdictions where physical delivery is restricted or impractical, subject to lawful market access, counterparty eligibility, sanctions screening, documented underlying exposure, and applicable MiFID II, EMIR, and bank documentation requirements.Cross-currency swaps or currency swaps for recurring or longer-term currency funding and liability management, subject to ISDA or equivalent master documentation, collateral and valuation terms, accounting treatment, and counterparty credit limits.Foreign-exchange options, collars, and structured hedges may be used for genuine commercial exposures only after assessment of complexity, loss profile, suitability, valuation, early-termination, and collateral risks; speculative trading should be prohibited under the treasury policy.Spot foreign-exchange transactions for settlement and operational conversion, with documented rate quotes, segregation of duties, authorized counterparties, and reconciliation to the underlying commercial payment.

E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: Medium for payment accounts, collections, SEPA transfers, foreign-exchange execution, and card services; low as a substitute for a full Spanish commercial-bank relationship. An EEA electronic-money institution or payment institution may provide services in Spain through passporting, subject to its home-state authorization, AML controls, safeguarding requirements, and permitted-service scope. An EMI does not provide ordinary bank deposits, deposit-guarantee protection, or necessarily a Spanish IBAN. Offshore non-EEA digital EMIs generally cannot provide regulated payment services into Spain without an appropriate EU authorization, branch, agent, or other lawful basis. The company should maintain a regulated Spanish or EEA bank account for tax payments, payroll, customs, trade-finance support, and counterparties requiring bank-grade evidence.

Statutory Filing Calendar

Modelo 390 – Annual VAT summary return (Declaración-resumen anual del IVA) On or before 30 January of the year following the reporting calendar year; mandatory electronic filing $0 USD Late filing triggers LGT art. 27 surcharge of 5%–20% of the net VAT due plus late-payment interest; inflating input VAT credits or refund claims is penalized at 50% of the excess; wilful non-filing constitutes an art. 198 LGT infringement carrying a penalty of 50%–150% of the tax damage (minimum EUR 300, or EUR 1,500 where the omitted assessment exceeds EUR 3,000).
Modelo 347 – Annual statement of transactions with third parties exceeding EUR 3,005.06 1–28 February (29 February in leap years) following the reporting calendar year; mandatory electronic filing $0 USD Per LGT art. 200, a fine of EUR 200 for each omitted or inaccurate transaction block, subject to a statutory minimum of EUR 200 and maximum of EUR 20,000 per declaration; if the omission is repeated for two consecutive years or involves survival-price evidence, the infringement may be upgraded and penalized up to EUR 60,000.
Modelo 200 – Annual corporate income tax return (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) Within the 25 calendar days following the six-month post-close period — for a 31 December fiscal year-end, from 1 July to 25 July of the following year $0 USD Late filing surcharge per LGT art. 27: 5% where filed within 3 months, 10% within 6 months, 15% within 12 months, and 20% plus annual late-payment interest after 12 months; wilful non-filing leads to AEAT official assessment with a penalty of 50%–150% of the assessed tax, a minimum penalty of EUR 1,500, and publication in the tax-defaulters' list under art. 95 LGT.

Strike-off trigger

Mandatory Audit Threshold Mandatory Audit for All Entities

Turnover: Mandatory independent statutory audit (art. 263 Ley de Sociedades de Capital, as amended by Ley 22/2015) applies when the SL meets at least two of the following three thresholds for two consecutive fiscal years: total assets exceeding EUR 2,850,000; net annual turnover exceeding EUR 5,700,000; or an average workforce exceeding 50 employees. Any SL that forms part of a consolidated group, receives public subsidies above the legal caps, or carries out securitization or special transactions is also subject to audit regardless of size.

Stage 06

Corporate Tax & Transfer Pricing

Corporate income tax (CIT), box-by-box return breakdown, dividend WHT, and director personal liability.

Statutory corporate income tax (CIT)

25% general rate (art. 29.1 Ley 27/2014, LIS). Reduced rates: 17% from FY2025 (23% in FY2024) for entities with annual net turnover below EUR 1,000,000; 15% for newly created SLs in the first two tax periods with a positive taxable base (art. 29.3 LIS); 15% for certified startups (Ley 28/2022) for the first four tax periods.

Dividend withholding tax (WHT)

19% statutory withholding (art. 25.1.f) Real Decreto Legislativo 5/2004, IRNR) on dividends paid by the Spanish SL to non-resident shareholders without a permanent establishment. 0% where the EU/EEA parent holds at least 5% of the capital for an uninterrupted one-year period (EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive as transposed); treaty rates typically 5%-10% for qualifying holdings, e.g., Spain-China DTA 5% (>=25% holding) or 10%; Spain-Hong Kong DTA 5% (>=25%) or 10%.

Mandatory Return Breakdown

Deadline: · Frequency:

Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the fiscal year-end. For a calendar-year SL: 1-25 July of the following year (e.g., FY2024 return due 1-25 July 2025).

Deadline: · Frequency:

First 20 calendar days of April (period 1), October (period 2) and December (period 3) for calendar-year entities.

Deadline: · Frequency:

Same deadline as Modelo 200: 25 calendar days following six months after fiscal year-end (1-25 July for calendar-year SL).

Box-by-Box Return Breakdown (non-resident focus)

BoxField Non-resident guidanceTax-evasion pitfall
Casilla 559 Base imponible (taxable base) after offset of prior-year negative tax bases. Attach reconciliation of accounting profit to taxable base in the annexes. Applicable to the Spanish-resident SL. A foreign parent operating through a Spanish permanent establishment files Modelo 200 on the PE income and attaches home-country tax residence certificate in the annex. Late-filing surcharge (recargo) of 5% to 20% escalating with delay plus late-payment interest (arts. 26-27 LGT); proportional sanction of 50% of the omitted amount (minimum EUR 1,000) for inaccurate returns (art. 191 LGT); formal-infraction fines EUR 200 to EUR 1,500 per box; criminal tax evasion threshold of EUR 120,000 per fiscal year (art. 305 Penal Code) with imprisonment of 1-5 years.
Casilla 562 Cuota integra (gross tax liability) computed by applying the applicable statutory rate to the taxable base; include the reduced 17%/23%/15% rates where eligible. No special non-resident entry; the SL computes at Spanish rates. Non-resident shareholders never report here; their dividend income is taxed under IRNR and reported in Modelo 210/216. Late-filing surcharge (recargo) of 5% to 20% escalating with delay plus late-payment interest (arts. 26-27 LGT); proportional sanction of 50% of the omitted amount (minimum EUR 1,000) for inaccurate returns (art. 191 LGT); formal-infraction fines EUR 200 to EUR 1,500 per box; criminal tax evasion threshold of EUR 120,000 per fiscal year (art. 305 Penal Code) with imprisonment of 1-5 years.
Casilla 577 Bonificaciones (tax allowances), e.g., 99% allowance for ETVE and 50% for income from qualifying intangible exports; leave zero for ordinary hotpot-base trading. ETVE allowance only where the SL qualifies and meets management-substance conditions; otherwise the AEAT will reclassify the benefit as a sham. Late-filing surcharge (recargo) of 5% to 20% escalating with delay plus late-payment interest (arts. 26-27 LGT); proportional sanction of 50% of the omitted amount (minimum EUR 1,000) for inaccurate returns (art. 191 LGT); formal-infraction fines EUR 200 to EUR 1,500 per box; criminal tax evasion threshold of EUR 120,000 per fiscal year (art. 305 Penal Code) with imprisonment of 1-5 years.
Casilla 579 Deducciones for R&D, innovation, film and cultural production, and deductions to avoid double taxation; enter documentation references to Form 200 annexes. Credits are computed at the SL level only; the SL may not pass credits to foreign shareholders. Late-filing surcharge (recargo) of 5% to 20% escalating with delay plus late-payment interest (arts. 26-27 LGT); proportional sanction of 50% of the omitted amount (minimum EUR 1,000) for inaccurate returns (art. 191 LGT); formal-infraction fines EUR 200 to EUR 1,500 per box; criminal tax evasion threshold of EUR 120,000 per fiscal year (art. 305 Penal Code) with imprisonment of 1-5 years.
Casilla 599 Cuota diferencial (tax payable after deducting instalments, withholdings and on-account payments). Negative amount generates refund or credit. If the SL has paid Modelo 216 withholdings on outbound dividends, those remain credits of the SL, not of the foreign recipient. Late-filing surcharge (recargo) of 5% to 20% escalating with delay plus late-payment interest (arts. 26-27 LGT); proportional sanction of 50% of the omitted amount (minimum EUR 1,000) for inaccurate returns (art. 191 LGT); formal-infraction fines EUR 200 to EUR 1,500 per box; criminal tax evasion threshold of EUR 120,000 per fiscal year (art. 305 Penal Code) with imprisonment of 1-5 years.
Casilla 632 Retenciones e ingresos a cuenta suffered by the SL on its own income (interest, royalties, Spanish dividends), reconciled with Modelo 193/123 certificates. Foreign shareholders' Spanish-source withholding is not attributable to the SL; the SL must verify its own withholding certificates. Late-filing surcharge (recargo) of 5% to 20% escalating with delay plus late-payment interest (arts. 26-27 LGT); proportional sanction of 50% of the omitted amount (minimum EUR 1,000) for inaccurate returns (art. 191 LGT); formal-infraction fines EUR 200 to EUR 1,500 per box; criminal tax evasion threshold of EUR 120,000 per fiscal year (art. 305 Penal Code) with imprisonment of 1-5 years.
Casilla 411 Resultado de la declaracion del ultimo periodo impositivo (prior-year tax liability) used as the base for the default instalment calculation method (Modalidad A). The instalment base is the SL's own prior-year liability; no direct non-resident cross-reference. Non-filing or underpayment triggers the 5%-20% surcharge plus interest (arts. 27 and 26 LGT); deliberate understatement attract the 50% proportional sanction; non-presentation of Modelo 202 also precludes deduction of the instalment in Modelo 200.
Casilla 415 Base del pago fraccionado: choose Modalidad A (5%/25% of prior-year liability for 2024-2025) or Modalidad B (taxable base of the year-to-date period with 17%/21% coefficient for large entities). Non-resident shareholders should verify that the SL uses Modalidad A to avoid over-payment disputes on repatriation cash flow. Non-filing or underpayment triggers the 5%-20% surcharge plus interest (arts. 27 and 26 LGT); deliberate understatement attract the 50% proportional sanction; non-presentation of Modelo 202 also precludes deduction of the instalment in Modelo 200.
Casilla 416 Importe del pago fraccionado (amount due). Payments are made by the SL from Spanish bank accounts; no foreign wire accepted for instalment settlements. Non-filing or underpayment triggers the 5%-20% surcharge plus interest (arts. 27 and 26 LGT); deliberate understatement attract the 50% proportional sanction; non-presentation of Modelo 202 also precludes deduction of the instalment in Modelo 200.
Casilla 418 Resultado a ingresar o a compensar after offsetting previous instalments (when using Modalidad B). Any negative result is automatically applied at the annual Modelo 200 filing; no refund is triggered. Non-filing or underpayment triggers the 5%-20% surcharge plus interest (arts. 27 and 26 LGT); deliberate understatement attract the 50% proportional sanction; non-presentation of Modelo 202 also precludes deduction of the instalment in Modelo 200.
Identificacion de la entidad vinculada Name, NIF/VAT number and country of each related counterparty (parent, sister, non-resident sales agent). Include all non-resident related purchasers of the hotpot soup base, e.g., Hong Kong distributor; foreign entity needs a Spanish NIF or passport/local tax ID; attach TRC where used for treaty rate application. Fine of EUR 1,000 per omitted transaction and EUR 5,000 per group of incorrect data (art. 198 LGT); false or incomplete TP documentation additionally triggers a 50%-150% assessment on the adjusted tax quota under art. 191 LGT.
Tipos y montantes de operaciones Aggregate per related party: sales of goods, royalties, management fees, loans, and intragroup services, with amounts expressed in EUR. Report intercompany sales at the invoice value before WHT; separately flag deemed-dividend reclassification items. Fine of EUR 1,000 per omitted transaction and EUR 5,000 per group of incorrect data (art. 198 LGT); false or incomplete TP documentation additionally triggers a 50%-150% assessment on the adjusted tax quota under art. 191 LGT.
Metodos de valoracion Arm's-length method applied per transaction category (CUP, resale minus, cost plus, TNMM, profit split). For export sales to related non-resident distributors, describe CUP benchmark based on quoted tallow / soup-base export prices or a comparable third-party distributor margin. Fine of EUR 1,000 per omitted transaction and EUR 5,000 per group of incorrect data (art. 198 LGT); false or incomplete TP documentation additionally triggers a 50%-150% assessment on the adjusted tax quota under art. 191 LGT.
Documentacion de soporte Reference to the contemporaneous Local File / Master File and update of economic analysis. Non-resident parent must provide its Master File segment showing group functions, assets and risks attributable to the Spanish SL. Fine of EUR 1,000 per omitted transaction and EUR 5,000 per group of incorrect data (art. 198 LGT); false or incomplete TP documentation additionally triggers a 50%-150% assessment on the adjusted tax quota under art. 191 LGT.

Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: Mandatory contemporaneous Local File and Master File where the Spanish SL's annual net turnover equals or exceeds EUR 10,000,000 (art. 18.3 LIS and RD 634/2015). Entities below that threshold must still prepare simplified documentation when related-party transactions with a single counterparty exceed EUR 250,000; Modelo 232 must be filed for such transactions. The Master File is required where the consolidated group turnover equals or exceeds EUR 45,000,000 (or EUR 750,000,000 for financial/insurance entities).

Economic substance scope: Spain has no standalone Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) comparable to UAE/BCPS, but substance is enforced indirectly through: (i) the general anti-abuse clause (art. 15 LIS) allowing recharacterization of artificial structures; (ii) CFC rules (arts. 83-100 LIS) attributing passive income of controlled foreign entities to the Spanish shareholder; (iii) the 'place of effective management' test for corporate residence (art. 8.1.c) LIS); and (iv) ETVE requirements that the company have real management, personnel and premises in Spain. An SL with no employees, no office, and contracts concluded outside Spain is exposed to sham-vehicle reclassification, denial of treaty benefits, and a deemed dividend taxable at 25% IS plus 19% WHT.

Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

Tax Evasion - understating export receipts

Statutory sanction: Administrative: proportional fine of 50% to 150% of the omitted quota (art. 191 LGT) plus late-payment interest and 5%-20% recargo. Criminal (art. 305 Penal Code): where the defrauded quota exceeds EUR 120,000 per fiscal year, imprisonment of 1 to 5 years, a fine of 2 to 6 times the defrauded amount, and loss of subsidies and public benefits.

Director personal liability: De facto and de jure directors are subsidiarily liable for the unpaid corporate tax debt under art. 42.2 LGT where they failed to make the company comply with tax obligations; in criminal cases, the court may impose precautionary measures including passport seizure and travel bans, and lifting the corporate veil permits seizure of the director's personal assets for civil restitution.
Shell Company / Artificial Substance

Statutory sanction: Recharacterization under art. 15 LIS with the income reattributed to the ultimate foreign shareholder; CFC inclusion of passive income; denial of treaty benefits; administrative adjustment plus a 50% penalty; the AEAT may also impose 19% IRNR on the deemed dividend and interest surcharges.

Director personal liability: Directors face subsidiary liability under art. 42.2 LGT for the adjusted debt; in the criminal phase, travel bans and asset embargoes are commonly ordered; disqualification from managing Spanish companies may be imposed where the sham facilitated tax fraud.
Transfer Pricing Non-Compliance

Statutory sanction: TP adjustment to the arm's-length price; the underpriced margin is reclassified as a constructive dividend taxable at 25% IS plus 19% WHT on the deemed distribution; 50% penalty on the adjusted quota (art. 191 LGT); additional 25% penalty for non-presentation of Modelo 232.

Director personal liability: Where the director failed to maintain the contemporaneous documentation and caused the insolvency of the SL, the director is jointly and severally liable for the TP debt under art. 42.2 LGT; criminal liability under art. 305 may attach if the TP distortion exceeds EUR 120,000 and is intentional.
AML and Cash Payment Limits

Statutory sanction: Cash-payment breach: fine of 25% of the amount paid (art. 34 Ley 7/2012); AML administrative infringement under Ley 10/2010: fines up to EUR 5,000,000 for serious infractions; criminal money-laundering charges (art. 301 Penal Code) where funds originate from tax evasion, with imprisonment of 6 months to 6 years.

Director personal liability: The compliance officer and managing director are personally liable for AML fines as the 'sujeto obligado' and its legal representative; prohibitions on leaving Spain, freezing orders and travel bans are available in money-laundering investigations; the criminal liability is personal and cannot be discharged by the SL's liquidation.
